merger_name: The Disability Trust - LEAD Disability Services
merger_description:
The Disability Trust Limited (**The Disability Trust**) is a public benevolent institution, registered with the Australian Charities and Not-for-profits Commission. It is a registered National Disability Insurance Scheme (**NDIS**) provider and operates in New South Wales, the Australian Capital Territory, Victoria and Queensland. The Disability Trust offers individualised services such as accommodation support, employment assistance, community engagement programs facilitating social activities, group participation and therapy and support services. The Disability Trust is part of the Meridia group.

Lead Disability Services Ltd (**LEAD**) is a public benevolent institution, registered with the Australian Charities and Not-for-profits Commission. LEAD has a particular interest in providing community participation, employment and training services to people who have a disability. LEAD also operates a Registered Training Organisation delivering vocational education that supports people to build careers in disability, aged care, and community services. LEAD is a registered NDIS provider and operates in New South Wales and the Australian Capital Territory.

Both The Disability Trust and LEAD operate an Australian Disability Enterprise (**ADE**). ADEs are not-for-profit organisations with charitable status which provide employment for people with significant disability who would otherwise encounter barriers to obtaining employment.

The Disability Trust proposes to become the sole member of LEAD (the **Acquisition**).

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition given:
a. there is a small horizontal overlap between The Disability
Trust (and its connected entities) and LEAD in the supply of
disability support services, including NDIS employment
support services, in New South Wales and the Australian
Capital Territory
b. there are alternative suppliers of disability support services,
including NDIS employment support services, in New South
Wales and the Australian Capital Territory.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
